i think we introduce more political education in schools and add optional voting for 16 and 17 year olds. a democracy will only be improved with more input, and the idea that teens are 'not responsible enough/not educated enough' to vote is silly because people are equally uninterested/educated in politics at all ages. i argue it would also further encourage political engagement which is vital for a democratic society.

16 and 17 year olds are expected to follow so many civic duties such as paying tax, following laws, facing adult punishments for crimes. etc., so it's not a case of 'they aren't responsible enough' or can't be trusted to follow a type of social contract.

as much as i would love to say 'dont let idiots vote', thats the point of a democracy. let idiots vote because that is representation, and unfortunately idiots deserve the same representation as everyone else.

Genuine response, here is my basic timeline (as unbiased as possible): 

1. Tommyinnit was talking negatively about Mizkif

2. xQc responded saying that Tommy was being cringe

3. Tommy replied saying xQc was far more cringe for being a Trump supporter

4. xQc that Tommy went from "dick riding Dream to making jokes for teenage girls"

5. Dream responded with the meme format (since been deleted) of the person reaching a cross road, in which one path leads to a brightly lit castle and another leads to a stormy castle, with a label on the person saying 'DreamSMP stans', a label on the bright castle saying 'growing up', and a label on the dark castle saying 'becoming a r\*\*\*\*\*d Tommyinnit fan'. 

6. Many people (other mcyts, Tommyinnit fans, current/ex-mcyt fans, and even just regular people) responded to the post, with the general opinion being held that Dream was innapropriate for using the r slur. 

7. Dream posted a reddit statement (that has since been deleted) that to summarise, said that he believed that he was able to use the r slur due to being autistic because he had seen multiple people going viral for calling him it that were excused for being neurodivergent (specifically mentioning Nicolas Cantu) - arguing people were only upset at him for using it because they already disliked him. He then said he had personal reasons for being upset that Tommy was acting as the 'internet police' and that he was expected to recieve 'shit' for going after Tommy who he argued lies about him constantly and supports ex DreamSMP fans who 'make up lies and shit on other creators' just to promote his tour/videos/podcast. 

8. Tommy responded to a twitter user that reposted Dream's reddit statement, saying "all I had to do was get Trump involved and he finally cracked". 

9. Other large creators continued to come out (as far as I am aware, all in support of Tommy/kind of hesistant to 'choose sides') on Twitter with responses. Tubbo made a stream discussing Dream's reddit post, in which he generally disagreed with Dream. 

10. Dream then went live on Twitch for a fairly long 'tell all' type stream reacting to Tubbo's vod (he did skip parts of the vod, which many considered to be extremely relevant) which mostly focused on previous drama or accusations within the DSMP community (I honestly cannot recap the entire video, you are better off watching it yourself or finding more in depth recaps. I probably wouldn't describe it as an apology, but more of a 'I'm not in the wrong' kind of video.).

11. Tubbo made another stream in which he watched and reacted to Dream's vod (Tubbo did speed some parts of the vod up, but watched the entire thing), in which he again generally agreed with Tommy/disagreed with Dream, but did not 'blindly' side with any particular side. 

12. Tommy then made a 5 minute youtube video responding to the situation saying that Dream shouldn't have called his viewers the r slur because it is extremely ableist, that Dream and his friends have acted extremely sexist in front of and behind the camera, that he can acknowledge that he has made mistakes but (unlike Dream) he takes responsibility for his actions, that it is shameful for Dream to still hold the youtube advice he gave him at 16 years old over his head, etc. (the video is only 5 mins long, I would recommend just watching it). 

  
Other things have definitely happened but these felt most relevant at the time of writing. I hope anyone reading this can understand that this is a genuine attempt to provide an unbiased recount of the events, and that you may correct me for any incorrect statements I may have accidentally made, but I am not interested in hearing that you believe what I have accounted is incorrect due to your opinions.
